headline: [Most Wanted Caught!] Mexico Captures 'El Chapo Isidro', [11 Dead] in Firefight
sub: He was on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list
caption:
🚔 Most Wanted Caught! Mexico Captures 'El Chapo Isidro', 11 Dead in Firefight

Mexican forces captured alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro", in the city of Guasave in Sinaloa state. The raid began on Friday night and led to a deadly firefight.

🔹 Mexico's Defense Ministry said at least 11 people were killed: seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers.
🔹 He was one of the FBI's 10 Most Wanted fugitives, with a reward of up to $5 million. He is wanted in the U.S. on drug trafficking and firearms charges.
🔹 Burning vehicles blocked roads in Guasave after the arrest. Mexico's Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch said armed forces will stay deployed in Sinaloa.

💬 Will this arrest reduce cartel violence in Mexico? 👇

Sources: AP, CBS News

headline: [Gulf Attack!] Iran Fires Missiles and Drones at US Bases in [Bahrain]
sub: Bahrain says fire hit an industrial site
caption:
⚠️ Gulf Attack! Iran Fires Missiles and Drones at US Bases in Bahrain

Iran launched missile and drone attacks on Bahrain late on Saturday, saying it was targeting US military bases. Bahrain, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, said its air defences intercepted several Iranian attacks.

🔹 Bahrain's Interior Ministry said one attack caused a fire at a civilian industrial facility, with no injuries reported.
🔹 Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed they destroyed US Patriot air defence radars. Bahrain and the US military have not confirmed this.
🔹 Iran said the attack was a response to US drones entering its airspace. On the same day, at least three oil tankers were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz.

💬 Can talks stop the fighting in the Gulf? 👇

Sources: Al Jazeera, Euronews

headline: [167-Year Puzzle] Computer Check Backs AI-Assisted Proof of [Riemann Hypothesis]
sub: Maths groups say they have full confidence
caption:
🧮 167-Year Puzzle: Computer Check Backs AI-Assisted Proof of Riemann Hypothesis

Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in maths, with help from the company's AI model Claude. He posted the claim on Friday, and on Saturday two maths groups said a computer check of his proof found it correct.

🔹 The Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative reviewed the proof written in the Lean computer language and said they have "full confidence" it is correct.
🔹 Alpöge says Claude helped him build the solution over about six weeks. The problem was first posed in 1859.
🔹 The Clay Mathematics Institute's $1 million prize still requires publication and years of review by other mathematicians.

💬 Could AI help solve other big science mysteries? 👇

Sources: The Guardian, Bloomberg

#GlobalEye #RiemannHypothesis #Anthropic #Claude #AI #Mathematics
photo_needed: Levent Alpöge, face clearly visible (or the Anthropic logo / Claude logo sign, or a chalkboard with the Riemann zeta function). A big, clear, landscape photo works best.
